facts.text: The cast and crew were mostly undergrads at the University of Miami plus Miami locals, so this cannibal-pilgrim splatter comedy is basically a student-and-friends passion project.
This cannibal-pilgrim splatter comedy was made for a reported $10,000. Writer-director Erick Lorinc's feature debut leans on practical gore rather than a big effects budget.
Exteriors and a short film were shot in Chattanooga, Tennessee in November 2017, months before the main shoot began in Florida.
Cinematographer Nicholas Punales also acts in the film, playing the restaurant owner Mr. Pearl. He shot the movie and then stepped in front of the camera too.
Principal photography ran only on weekends, from March to May 2018, around Miramar, Hollywood and Miami, Florida. Derry's Family Restaurant in Hollywood served as the diner.
The film's production company is Peak Jerry Productions. Sean Parker of Horror Obsessive says its themes are gluttony, greed and consumerism, served up with a side of Pilgrim cannibalism.
Sean Parker at Horror Obsessive says the film's staff are workers at Derry's Famous Fish & Grits Diner, a fictional name for the real Hollywood, Florida restaurant where it was shot.
Scream queen Linnea Quigley (Return of the Living Dead, Night of the Demons) cameos as Paulette. Sean Parker at Horror Obsessive singled her performance out as a highlight.
Reviewer Eric at The Scariest Things noted that for at least half the cast this was a first IMDb credit. He gave the film 2.5 out of 5 stars.
Writer-director Erick Lorinc also appears on screen, as Ranger Ghouly, and edited the film himself.
Writer-director Erick Lorinc's relatives joined in: Jesse Lorinc plays the Dog, and Lorinc himself appears as Ranger Ghouly. Casting family and friends is a classic indie-horror move.
The film grew out of a short called Thanksgiving 1978, which was shot in Chattanooga in 2017. It runs about six minutes and was later included as an extra on the Blu-ray.
The film's villains, the Brimstons, claim descent from Pilgrims who supposedly ate people to survive the first Thanksgiving, according to a review by Eric at The Scariest Things.
Horror Fuel's Joseph Perry said the film delivers big time on practical-effects gore and gags, and singled out a memorable use of a whisk.
The Scariest Things' Eric called the movie's blood and gore 'stellar for a movie with this tiny budget' and praised the sound design for making the violence 'crunchy and squishy.'
Reviewers spotted nods to Blood Diner, Alice's Restaurant, I Know What You Did Last Summer, Friday the 13th Part 3 and Return of the Living Dead, per Sean Parker at Horror Obsessive.
Rotten Tomatoes lists critic Dennis Harvey calling it an 'enthusiastic shoestring holiday horror,' and Heather Wixson giving it 3 out of 5 as messy but a worthy Thanksgiving-horror addition.
Horror Fuel's Joseph Perry noted that director Erick Lorinc shows his love of horror with nods to John Carpenter and other filmmakers.
Horror Fuel's Joseph Perry said the film's jokes about Indigenous peoples, told by the villains, fall flat, though Lorinc has a protagonist correct them.
Critic Jessica Scott, in a Rotten Tomatoes-listed review, called the film's humor and look 'pitch perfect for a self-consciously goofy slasher throwback.'
The film premiered online during the COVID-19 pandemic, playing the Pasadena Horror Film Festival, American Horror Film Festival and Salem Horror Fest.
Sam Panico of Bands About Movies compared the cannibal family's home-invasion menace to The Strangers, and called horror legend Linnea Quigley 'that most perfect of slasher desserts.'
Scream Team Releasing put the film out on Blu-ray and on VHS in November 2020, fitting for a grindhouse-style cannibal movie.
The film played Another Hole in the Head Film Festival, held online December 11 to 27, 2020, after its Salem Horror Fest premiere that autumn.
AllMovie lists the film as unrated (NR) with an October 2, 2020 release date.
Sean Parker at Horror Obsessive reviewed it from Salem Horror Fest and called it 'so bad it's good', while praising the menacing mask worn by Michael Vitovich as Trip Brimston.
The film's credits list a separate performer, Molly Dominick, as 'Trip's Face,' beside Michael Vitovich as Trip Brimston, the masked Pilgrim killer.
